summary.title: Utonia: Toward One Encoder for All Point Clouds

details: Point-cloud self-supervised learning is domain-fragmented: naively mixing indoor, outdoor LiDAR, remote-sensing, and object-centric data destabilizes joint training because features latch onto domain-specific cues (scale/grid granularity, gravity-aligned z convention, availability of color/normal channels).

Utonia: a single self-supervised Point Transformer V3 encoder pretrained jointly across all these point-cloud domains via teacher-student self-distillation, with three minimal domain-agnostic fixes instead of domain-specific modules.

The three fixes: (1) causal modality blinding — randomly dropping color/normal channels per-sample and per-point so the encoder never treats modality availability as a shortcut; (2) perceptual granularity rescaling — rescaling every point cloud to one shared 'observation resolution' under a single global grid size, with gravity treated as a granularity-dependent prior (upright for scenes, full SO(3) for objects); (3) 3D RoPE applied to the granularity-aligned (and jittered/rescaled) coordinates in every attention layer as a continuous relative-geometry positional cue.

~250k cross-domain point clouds plus 1M sampled Cap3D CAD assets (90k Cap3D subsampled per epoch to balance the mixture); domains span indoor scans, outdoor LiDAR, remote sensing, object CAD, and video-lifted clouds.
Two-stage schedule: Stage 1 on curated high-quality ScanNet, Structured3D, Waymo, PartNet; Stage 2 continues 100 epochs on the full mixture.

Cross-modal joint prediction with paired images (as in Concerto) where available; outdoor colors projected from calibrated images (black otherwise); normals estimated with Open3D; video data lifted with provided cameras or VGGT.
Batch size 256 on 64 NVIDIA H20 GPUs; self-distillation upcast level set to 0.
PTv3 backbone, scaled 38M -> 137M; channel counts constrained to be divisible by 6 for separable 3D RoPE.
RoPE base B=10 (ablated over a wide range); DINOv3-style anisotropic coordinate jitter and isotropic rescale applied only to RoPE coordinates.
Augmentation asymmetry: scenes get ±10% scale jitter, full yaw and only ±pi/64 roll/pitch; objects get ±50% scale jitter and full SO(3) rotations.
Temporal frame augmentation for sequence data: teacher sees pose-aligned multi-frame aggregate, student a single frame.
Linear probing, decoder probing, and full fine-tuning (no PPT, trained directly on target datasets) under Sonata/Concerto protocols.

Indoor semantic segmentation (ScanNet, ScanNet200, ScanNet++, S3DIS), outdoor segmentation (incl. Waymo, nuScenes), object classification (ModelNet40, ScanObjectNN OBJ-BG and PB-T50-RS, no voting), part segmentation (ShapeNetPart, PartNetE).
Robustness tests with color and/or normal channels removed at inference.
Sonata and Concerto, retrained by the authors on domains they do not originally report (Sonata on objects; Concerto on outdoor and objects) for fair cross-domain comparison.
For the pilot study: per-domain default grid sizes and grid-size jittering versus unified grid plus granularity rescaling.

Robotic manipulation: simulated tabletop clutter grasping from monocular RGB-D (Objaverse-LVIS assets, 290 categories; expert data via BoDex/CuRobo, rendered in Isaac Sim), success rate over three attempts, conditioning a VLA policy.
Spatial reasoning: frozen Utonia features added to Video-3D LLM (LLaVA-Video-7B) visual tokens, evaluated on ScanRefer, Multi3DRefer, Scan2Cap, ScanQA, SQA3D.
Open-world part segmentation: replacing Sonata with Utonia as encoder in a P3SAM variant with a SAM-like promptable decoder, mIoU on PartObjaverse-Tiny.

key_findings.finding: Naive multi-domain joint pretraining fails, and the failure is traced to granularity/grid-size mismatch, gravity-convention bias, and inconsistent modality availability.
key_findings.evidence: Pilot experiments show joint training with per-dataset default grid sizes is unstable with large performance drops, and grid-size jittering gives only limited robustness; feature visualizations show Sonata and Concerto features exhibit strong z-correlated patterns, and cross-domain retrieval of a toy-car front fails to highlight the corresponding region of a real car in LiDAR.

key_findings.finding: Fixing a global grid size and rescaling coordinates to a shared perceptual granularity is what makes joint cross-domain training stable and transferable.
key_findings.evidence: In the scale/grid-size ablation, unified grid plus coordinate rescaling substantially improves both joint-training stability and cross-domain transfer relative to per-domain grids or grid jittering.

key_findings.finding: Applying RoPE on granularity-aligned coordinates consistently improves cross-domain point SSL, with the largest gains where density is most non-uniform.
key_findings.evidence: RoPE ablation shows consistent improvements on ScanNet200, Waymo, and PartNetE under multi-domain training, with the largest gain on outdoor Waymo; gains also appear under single-domain Waymo training, attributed to within-scan density non-uniformity. Performance is stable across a wide range of RoPE bases.

key_findings.finding: Causal modality blinding makes the encoder robust to missing color/normal channels, and applying the dropout at data loading is the most effective placement.
key_findings.evidence: With color or normals dropped on ScanNet and nuScenes, Concerto degrades substantially (especially without color) while Utonia remains stable; ablation shows blinding at data loading > local-views-only > masked-views (masked views are already information-limited).

key_findings.finding: Cross-domain joint pretraining becomes a net win rather than a competition only once model capacity is sufficient, and further data scaling adds gains.
key_findings.evidence: At 38M PTv3, multi-domain pretraining matches domain-specific models indoors and on objects but slightly lags outdoors; scaling to 137M makes multi-domain surpass domain-specific pretraining overall, and expanding from 83k to 250k+1M data further improves indoor and outdoor benchmarks (PartNetE fine-tuning improves while its linear probing drops).
